payload.friendly_name: Charter contract skeleton and Gradle build (retroactive)
payload.purpose_context: The charter contract skeleton and the Java 25 Gradle build were built in an earlier session under operator decisions of 2026-10-18 but skipped specify, plan and review. This mission states what was decided and built, checks it against those decisions, and tracks the open items still needed to call steps 1 and 2 done.
payload.purpose_tldr: Record, review and close out roadmap steps 1-2, which landed without the mission workflow.

options: Record, review and close open items
Record and review only; open items become follow-up missions
payload.question: What does done mean for this retroactive mission: record and review only, or also close the open items (core contract tooling, first Java 25 CI run, Java style check) inside it?

payload.final_answer: Record, review and close open items

payload.question: How are the three calls made without review settled: PACK_LEVEL_MISSING as a warning-level diagnostic, the provisional action-context rules, and the scenarios directory name?

payload.final_answer: Adversarial squad reviews each call at the plan point; operator then ratifies, amends or reverts, and the ruling is recorded

options: Keep contract scenarios beside the contract; #43 suites join them when bound
payload.question: Should #43's BDD layout (src/test/resources/features/, tests/scenarios/charter/) absorb contracts/charter/scenarios/?

payload.final_answer: Keep contract scenarios in contracts/charter/scenarios/; #43's suites move to contracts/charter/scenarios/<cluster>/ when their harness is bound, renamed for the terms guard, keeping #43's house style and promise tags

payload.question: Should the build produce Javadoc and publish it with the docsite?

payload.final_answer: Yes: Gradle javadoc for hand-written modules with doclint on and warnings failing; the Javadoc site is packaged by the main build workflow and published inside the docsite as a dedicated set of pages reached from the sidebar, styled to match the docsite

payload.question: Which style and formatting tools run in the build?

payload.final_answer: Checkstyle and Spotless with palantir-java-format

payload.question: Which static analysis runs at compile or check time?

payload.final_answer: Error Prone and NullAway with JSpecify

payload.question: Which test-quality libraries are added (AssertJ is already present)?

payload.final_answer: JaCoCo, PIT (pitest) and Mockito

payload.question: When does PIT mutation testing run?

payload.final_answer: Nightly, as an experiment; never on every pull request and never a merge gate

payload.question: Is jqwik used for property-based testing?

payload.final_answer: Rejected: jqwik carries an AI output clause (operator ruling 2026-10-18); an advisory issue goes to spec-kitty-open-packs

payload.question: Ruling on PACK_LEVEL_MISSING as a non-blocking diagnostic
Ruling on the provisional action-context rules
Ruling on the contracts/charter/scenarios directory and suite classpath
How does the contract pass core's lint and breaking check
Enable OpenRewrite?
Doclint missing-comment check: document every public member, or exclude missing
Which gates apply to test sources
File the upstream issues found by the squad

payload.final_answer: Ratify as is: keep the stricter Java behavior (diagnostic at every level and for an absent pack.yaml; pack_version required at every level), deliberately stricter than core. Log a remediation issue in spec-kitty-open-packs so that all packs adhere to the stricter enforcement.

Amend, rules to corpus: operation x-provisional (open decision: corpus #9), scenarios tagged @provisional; adopt core's sort; widen via to the node the edge starts from; keep dedup (pin the real DIRECTIVE_042 case) and the 404 for an action that is not a node of the graph, with the comparator mapping recorded; walk, activation filtering and load-error degrade recorded as provisional gaps decided by #9, with a scenario pinning today's load-error behavior.

Ratify the name and amend: only scenarios/** on the test classpath; contract scenarios selected by an @contract tag; fixtures stay inline as doc strings; FR-013 covers all three scenario homes (contract scenarios; #43 suites moved and bound atomically; tests/scenarios/charter acceptance scenarios with harness #31); every scenario change gets a contract CHANGELOG line; 'contract scenarios' is the canonical term.

Follow core's precedent: renumber to 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT with unstable parts x-provisional; all refusal and diagnostic codes snake_case like core's mission-status contract, Java maps through a token; PackLevel keeps built-in under one scoped, sunset ruleset deviation plus a core issue to amend enum-case; add the three descriptions; add x-source/x-derived citations to this repository's producers.
Do not enable OpenRewrite: not in the build, not in CI; evaluation recorded in research.md; revisit if Moderne's distribution changes.
Document everything: -Xdoclint:all with -Werror; every public type and member of the hand-written modules gets Javadoc in this mission.
Checkstyle, palantir formatting and Error Prone on main and test; NullAway and doclint on main only.

File: open-packs issue for stricter pack rules (pack.yaml with pack_level and pack_version at every level, folding in the qa pack.yaml and spk-internal-glossary stem defects); core issue to let enum-case accept built-in; core issue that the glossary contradicts code on PACK_LEVEL_MISSING; comment on charter #12 that ADR-0008 answered it, for the operator to close.

payload.question: How is the built-in enum-case conflict resolved without a local derived ruleset?

payload.final_answer: No local ruleset delta (it repeats the fork-and-drift mistake). Fix it in core: a PR for core #6402 so enum-case accepts the PackTier values, and a core PR so lint_check supports a consumer ruleset that extends core's (counting inherited rules). The charter runs core's ruleset unmodified; CORE_REF moves to the merged core commit; until then the lint step fails honestly on the one known violation. Supersedes the 'scoped, sunset ruleset deviation' part of DM 01M57SQD43YAX5Q3A6QNQBF1TT.

payload.question: How is the closed-response-objects convention enforced after five review rounds found holes in the Spectral rule?

payload.final_answer: Recursive checker in Java
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-10-18. Spectral's JSONPath rules cannot classify composed schemas (allOf/anyOf/oneOf, tuples, boolean schemas, constraint-only members) recursively; five review rounds each found a new hole. The closure convention moves to a small, unit-tested Java checker in the :contracts project that walks the bundled contract with a positive recursive classification and runs in check. The Spectral rule closed-response-objects is removed from contracts/lint/ruleset.yaml.
